description: What's enforced (machine-checked by schema/semantic_validate.py or extraction/verify_all.py) vs. convention-only (documentation, not enforced).
resolutionOrderNote: Genesis principle: never resolve aliases before the theme mode is known. This repo has one theme (light) so mode resolution is a no-op today, but the order is fixed for forward-compatibility if a dark theme is added later.

enforced.assetRoleEnum: schema/pagespec.schema.json assetRole enum + tokens/llm/component-allowlist.json parity, checked by extraction/verify_all.py
enforced.templateNodeSequence: schema/semantic_validate.py cross-references PageSpec.template against templates/templates.json's real node list
enforced.maxWordsBudgets: schema/semantic_validate.py counts words per content field against sections/*.json maxWords

conventionOnly.rawValueRestrictions: Section/component authors should reference semantic tokens in tokens/10-semantic/*.json rather than foundation hex/px values directly when writing NEW CSS; this is a style-guide convention for humans/future authors, not machine-checked, because PageSpec instances carry no raw style values at all (see overrides note below).

overrides.pageSpecTokenOverrideMechanism: NONE. Inspect schema/pagespec.schema.json and schema/example.pagespec.json: a PageSpec node has no per-instance style/token-override field. Styling is fully owned by the section/component contracts (sections/*.json, components/*.json), not by a generated PageSpec instance. This is a deliberate scope boundary (MASTER-GUIDE.md 3.21), not an oversight — do not add a fake override field just to have something to validate.
